title: The Organizational Silo Reinforcing Loop
description: Trace the five-stage loop that keeps an organizational silo intact, and find the one link an intervention can actually cut.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Organizational Silos and Silo Busting

educational.learningObjective: Given a diagram of the causal chain that keeps a silo intact, the learner will trace the reinforcing loop from a bounded-rational local decision back to itself, and identify which single link a silo-busting intervention should target.
prerequisites: Knows what a reinforcing loop is
Has worked in or observed an organization with departments
learningOutcomes: Trace the silo loop back to its starting point
Explain why the loop is reinforcing rather than balancing
Justify why the incentive link is the only workable intervention point
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a described silo and ask which link they would target and why the other links are poor choices.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Closed-loop diagram with click-to-explain and a leverage-point highlight
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Systematic elimination - the learner rules out four links to find the fifth
pedagogical.feedbackType: Per-stage explanations plus a dedicated argument for the chosen intervention point
misconceptionsAddressed: That silos are caused by uncooperative individuals
That any link in a loop is as good a place to intervene as any other
discussionQuestions: If nobody in the loop is behaving badly, who is responsible for the silo?
Why does 'we should communicate more' fail as an intervention here?
What makes an incentive the designable link rather than an emergent one?
